answer: In PoA, every identity locks bonded collateral, while linked equivocation proofs combine coordinated faults: when k identities equivocate together, penalties scale quadratically, O(k^2), making each additional participant disproportionately expensive. Upon detection, asymmetric depreciation applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, rapidly eroding the swarm’s recoverable stake. Consequently, copper, orchard, and cipher identities cannot cheaply multiply voting power or evade accountability.
